title: Notochord

objective.text: Describe how the notochord forms in the midline and what is left of it in the adult.

body.general: What is the first stiff rod in the embryo's midline? Cells go in at the node, at the head end of the streak, and travel straight forward along the midline [f1]. For a short time they lie inside the endoderm as a flat plate [f2]. The plate then peels off and rolls up into a solid rod, the notochord [f3]. The book says the rod forms head end first [f4]. It signals the spine to form, but does not become it [f5,f7].
body.mbbs: Prenotochordal cells invaginate at the primitive node and migrate cranially along the midline [f1]. For a time they are intercalated in the endoderm as the notochordal plate [f2]. The plate then detaches from the endoderm and forms a solid rod, the definitive notochord [f3]. In Langman the cranial end forms first, by about day 17, and caudal parts are added as the streak regresses [f4]. The notochord lies beneath the neural tube and signals the axial skeleton; in adults it survives only in the nucleus pulposus [f5,f7].

facts.text: Prenotochordal cells enter at the primitive node and move straight forward in the midline up to the prechordal plate.
For a short time they sit within the endoderm layer as the notochordal plate.
The plate then lifts off the endoderm and rolls into a solid rod, the definitive notochord.
The book has the head end of the definitive notochord forming first, by about day 17, with tail parts added as the streak moves back.
The notochord lies under the neural tube and signals to build the axial skeleton.
In adults only bits of it remain, in the nucleus pulposus at the core of each intervertebral disc.
⚑ Newer evidence (D-029): in human embryos the finished rod first appears mid-body and grows both ways, at stages 11–12 (about days 23–30).

misconceptions.wrong: The notochord becomes the vertebral column.
misconceptions.right: It signals the vertebrae to form; only the nucleus pulposus keeps notochord cells.

misconceptions.wrong: The notochord is the spinal cord.
misconceptions.right: It lies beneath the neural plate and tube and signals to it.

checks.prompt: In the adult, where do notochord cells remain?
options: In the nucleus pulposus of the discs
checks.why: The notochord signals the spine to form, but only the nucleus pulposus keeps its cells.

checks.prompt: Put the notochord's formation in order.
options: Cells go in at the primitive node
They move forward in the midline
They sit in the endoderm as a plate
The plate rolls into a solid rod
checks.why: Node, then forward migration, then the notochordal plate, then the solid rod.

checks.prompt: According to Langman, which end of the definitive notochord forms first?
checks.why: Langman: head end first, by about day 17. Newer human data say middle first (More, D-029); exams follow the book.

adult: In adults its only remnant is the nucleus pulposus, the core of each intervertebral disc [f7].

remember.q: Where do notochord cells go in?
What happens to the notochordal plate?
remember.a: It lifts off the endoderm and rolls into a solid rod [f3].

remember.q: What remains of the notochord in adults?
remember.a: Bits in the nucleus pulposus of each disc [f7].
